title: Critical WordPress Plugin Bugs Let Attackers Reset Admin Passwords and Take Over Sites
content_md: Two critical, unauthenticated vulnerability chains in The Events Calendar WordPress plugin could let remote attackers reset administrator passwords, execute operating-system commands, and take over vulnerable websites. The vulnerabilities affect The Events Calendar, a widely used WordPress plugin installed on more than 600,000 sites. StellarWP, the plugin’s developer, has released fixes, and administrators are urged to update to version 6.17.4.1 immediately. The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-78006 and CVE-2026-78159, each carry a CVSS severity score of 9.8 out of 10. Critical WordPress Plugin Bugs CVE-2026-78006 affects plugin versions up to and including 6.17.4 and enables unauthenticated PHP object injection that can lead to remote code execution. Attackers can abuse unsafe deserialization behavior to trigger a gadget chain within the plugin and execute arbitrary commands on the underlying web server. The second flaw, CVE-2026-78159, affects versions up to and including 6.17.3. It stems from inadequate validation of a widget classes map and can enable arbitrary PHP callable invocation. Rather than directly executing a system command, attackers can invoke WordPress functions with attacker-controlled arguments. Researchers demonstrated that this route could be used to invoke the wp_update_user() function and reset the password for administrator account ID 1.
